subject: Routing & Failover Playbook — pinning / auto-fallback ask for SLA coverage
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha@vectorcloud.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@vectorcloud.com
Date: 2026-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: how redwood handles routing failover during A/B for SLA commitments

Hey Tessa —

Quick context: VectorCloud is in the final stages of operational sign-off for the deal tied to VC-2025-045. Our uptime commitment to our customers requires documented failover guarantees during staged pushes (canary / A-B). Legal asked for a short note on how Redwood handles automatic fallback, forced pinning of model versions, and routing during capacity degradation so we can include it in the SOW.

Specific asks from our side:
- When a canary shows elevated 95th percentile latency or error spike, does Redwood provide an automatic fallback to the previous stable model variant?
- Can we request a hard pin of traffic to a specific model version for a time window (e.g., hold on v3.2 for 2 hours) while mitigation occurs?
- If a region hits capacity, how does routing escalate (cross-region vs cross-tier vs degrade to lower-cost model)?
- What operational playbook and logs will you provide so we can show auditors the actual rollback event and timeline?

If you can share a concise playbook or example flow, that would help close the procurement review today.

Thanks —
Asha
Director, Cloud Ops
VectorCloud

Subject: Re: Request: how redwood handles routing failover during A/B for SLA commitments

Hi Asha —

Thanks for the clear list. I'll put a concise playbook together and attach the internal routing/failover doc for your reviewers. Short answers up front:

- Automatic fallback: yes — Redwood can be configured to auto-fallback to a pinned stable variant when SLO/thresholds are breached for the canary cohort. This is rule-driven and tied to the rollout policy (we'll include conditions).
- Forced pin: yes — we support manual or API-driven pinning of a model version for a specified TTL. This can be applied globally or per-route.
- Capacity routing: policy-driven: prefer same-region, then cross-region within the same tier, then fallback to a compatible, lower-cost model variant if configured. You can opt-out of cross-region routing in Private deployments.
- Evidence: we provide a timeline (console trace), token-level latency and error metrics, and an event audit trail (who triggered pin/fallback, timestamp).

Attaching a draft redwood-routing-playbook-v1.pdf and an SLO exception request form (slo-exception-request-VC-045.docx) for procurement.

Marissa / Aditya — tagging you for the recommended rollout thresholds and whether we should include automated KV cache invalidation as part of the fallback play.

Next step for VectorCloud: review the attached playbook and tell me what level of automation you want (manual guardrail vs fully automatic). I can also spin up a runbook example showing a simulated canary rollback.

— Tessa

Subject: Re: Request: how redwood handles routing failover during A/B for SLA commitments

Asha / team —

Adding the ops-prescribed thresholds we typically recommend for enterprise SLAs:

- Canary sample size: 5–10% of traffic or min 250 requests over 15 minutes (whichever hits first).
- Immediate auto-fallback trigger: 95th percentile latency > baseline + 150ms sustained for 3 consecutive 60s windows OR error rate increase > 1.5x baseline for 2 windows.
- Soft-guard rails: alert + hold rollout at 5% increments if latency increases > baseline + 100ms.

Operational behavior: when the auto-fallback condition triggers, the orchestrator will do the following in order (configurable):
1) Mark canary cohort as failed and stop ramping.
2) Re-route new requests for the canary cohort to the last stable variant (pinned or previous rollout).
3) Optionally invalidate prefix/KV caches for the canary cohort (recommended if prompt shaping changed).
4) Emit an audit event and create a rollback timeline entry in the Console (includes token-level metrics and traces).

Pin policy: we support pin TTLs (1h/4h/24h) and indefinite until manually released. When pinned, the routing table will prefer the pinned variant and disallow automated promotion of newer variants for the pinned route.

Notes on cross-region: by default we prefer same-region fallback. If capacity is exhausted we will (if allowed) route to a compatible variant in another region. If VectorCloud requires a strict same-region SLA, we'll disable cross-region failover in the policy.

For auditors: we can give a PDF of the console event log for the exact timeframe of a rollback. If Vault/KMS evidence is needed for keys, Laura can attach the key rotation and access logs.

I attached a trimmed playbook and a sample JSON snippet for the rollout policy you can paste into your CD pipeline.

— Marissa

Quick engineering caveat for VectorCloud:

- Automatic fallback is gated by model compatibility. If you route from a quantized variant to a full-precision one, we attempt to maintain output shape/format but may change tokenization edge cases. We'll list compatible fallback targets in the policy.
- For high throughput customers we recommend a small warmup window for cross-tier fallback so KV cache priming doesn't cause transient latency spikes. Our default warmup is 90s.
- Pinning is implemented at the route-layer and will block autoscaling-based reallocation that would evict the pinned instance unless an admin override is used. That can have capacity implications — we'll surface that in the SLO exception form (included).

If VectorCloud wants, we can add a clause in the SOW about required concurrency buffer sizing for pinned routes to ensure we meet 99.9% uptime with the mailbox of pinned variants.

— Aditya

Asha —

Thanks for the quick review. Per your procurement timeline, here's what we will deliver for the SOW appendix:

1) One-page routing & rollback playbook (attached) that documents automatic fallback conditions, pin TTL options, and cross-region behavior.
2) Audit evidence bundle: console event timeline + PDF export for any rollback events.
3) Engineering caveats and recommended concurrency buffer for pinned routes (to be included as a short note in SOW).
4) SLO exception form filled with the proposed thresholds above — we will mark cross-region fallback as opt-in.

Please confirm whether you want auto-fallback to run fully automated or to be gated by a human approval step. If you pick human gate, procurement will want the exact SLA of the manual ticket-to-action time (we typically quote a 15–30 minute median response for on-call).

If all good, I'll have legal-ready language and the filled form over by EOD and cc: Laura for the key/access logs.
